## Overview {#sec-overview}

Tobacco usage has been found to be linked to numerous medical diseases and conditions, one of which is poor oral health \[[1](https://www.fda.gov/tobacco-products/health-effects-tobacco-use/how-tobacco-use-affects-oral-health)\]. The primary objective of this project is to explore the potential association that smoking has on periodontal disease among adults. It will include tobacco use trends in Philadelphia to highlight public health awareness at the local level. The data that will be used for this project comes from a 2011-12 NHANES database on the periodontic aspect of oral health through the R package “ForCausality”.

Dr. Kei Katsura, a Post Doc at CHOP, and Dr. Mohammad Abukar, a professor at Temple University Dental School, were both consulted to aid with identifying potential topics and the types of analyses to be done with the dataset. I also learned a great deal about how secondhand inhalation of smoking can cause an increased risk in oral health problems.

Repo Link: <https://github.com/DannyTran0/BMIN5030_Final_Project>

## Introduction {#sec-introduction}

Periodontal disease is a broad condition where bacterial infections and/or inflammatory responses affect gum and bone tissues surrounding and supporting teeth \[[2](https://www.cdc.gov/oral-health/about/gum-periodontal-disease.html)\]. While it can be preventable, it can be destructive if left untreated \[[2](https://www.cdc.gov/oral-health/about/gum-periodontal-disease.html)\]. There are numerous factors that can cause periodontal disease, but this project will focus on the use of tobacco in smoking. Due to the nature of tobacco being burned while smoking, it has been linked to negatively impacting oral health among other health complications \[[1](https://www.fda.gov/tobacco-products/health-effects-tobacco-use/how-tobacco-use-affects-oral-health)\]. Non-smokers are also affected through secondhand smoke exposure which increases risk of health complications especially among children and the elderly \[[3](https://www.cdc.gov/tobacco/about/index.html)\]. 

Despite trends in the smoking rate decreasing nationally between 2012-2022 among adults, Philadelphia has consistently remained above the national rate \[[4](https://www.phila.gov/media/20250114150429/CHARTe9v2a_Tobacco-Trends.pdf)\]. Public health support and resources are needed to educate the residents on the dangers of smoking. In turn, smokers would be able to find the help needed to quit smoking.

This project aims to explore the potential association between smoking and periodontal disease measurements among adults. In particular, it will explore how various demographic factors, income, and the number of cigarettes smoked per day is correlated with causing periodontal disease. This is where the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) data for 2011-12 comes into play to aid with the analysis. Additionally, it will examine tobacco use in Philadelphia to provide context on the local level with public health.

The project is interdisciplinary as it connects various fields on the issue of smoking as a cause for periodontal disease, including dentistry, biomedical data science, public health, behavioral psychology, and sociology. As such, reaching out to experts in these fields is essential to understand the problem. The following experts were consulted:

- Dr. Kei Katsura: During our conversations, she helped me with formulating and refining my research topic for the project while also describing how I could utilize the different variables to aid with analyzing the data. She had mentioned that due to the “race” variable being too broad, I should be cautious with the conclusions being made as it does not state other races.

- Dr. Mohammad Abukar: During our conversation, we discussed ways to go about analyzing the dataset, suggesting tying in how age, gender, race, and income could cause an individual to turn to smoking and subsequently getting periodontal disease. He also suggested the possibility that I use the analyzed data to apply it to the city of Philadelphia to see which areas are more prone to tobacco use and make a case for spreading awareness about smoking dangers.

## Methods {#sec-methods}

Two datasets will be used for this project. The primary dataset, which assess the number of periodontal disease measurements based on if the participant in a smoker, is from the 2011-12 NHANES on oral health (periodontal) conducted by the Center for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC). All of the data will be used. The other dataset is from the 2014 and 2017 Census Tract-level Data of 500 U.S. cities provided from the CDC's Division of Population Health, Epidemiology and Surveillance Branch. Model-based estimates on smoking use from Philadelphia and its geographical coordinates data will be used.

#### Package Requirements

Starting off, it is important to install the necessary R packages for use. Below is code that installs the R package `ForCausality` which contains the primary dataset that this project will be using. Including `ForCausality`, various other R packages will be called to aid in analyzing and visualizing the data.

```{r}
#| eval: FALSE

install.packages("ForCausality")
```

```{r}
#| label: load-packages

library(ForCausality)
library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)
library(modelsummary)
library(sf)
library(RColorBrewer)
library(tidycensus)
library(leaflet)
library(ggspatial)
library(tigris)

options(tigris_use_cache=T)
```

#### Periodontal Data Processing

First, the primary dataset will be loaded into a variable through a function called "Periodontal_df."

```{r}
#Loads primary dataset
periodontal.data<-Periodontal_df
#Views dataset
head(periodontal.data)
```

Despite the package providing processed data, most of it are vague and do not have much meaning. As such, it will be modified to provide proper meaning to the data, one example being the conversion of 0 and 1 from the gender variable to indicate male and female. Smoker status will also be converted and age will be categorized into various age groups. Additionally, the majority of the variable names will be renamed.

```{r}
#Data modifications
periodontal.data<-rename(periodontal.data, #Renames variables to provide more concrete meaning to what data means
                         id=SEQN,
                         gender=female,
                         race=black,
                         education=educf,
                         peri.detected=either,  #Number of detected periondontal disease measurements
                         peri.not.detected=neither, #No detected periodontal disease measurement
                         percent.peri.detected=pcteither,
                         smoker.status=z,
                         pair=mset) |>
#Modifies and categorizes gender data
  mutate(gender=factor(gender,levels=c(1,0),
                       labels=c("female","male"))) |>
#Modifies and categorizes age data
  mutate(age=case_when(                       
    age>=30 & age<40 ~ "30-40",
    age>=40 & age<50 ~ "40-50",
    age>=50 & age<60 ~ "50-60",
    age>=60 & age<70 ~ "60-70",
    age>=70 & age<80 ~ "70-80",
  )) |>
#Modifies and categorizes race data
  mutate(race=factor(race,levels=c(1,0),      
                     labels=c("African American","Other"))) |>
#Modifies and categorizes smoker status data
  mutate(smoker.status=factor(smoker.status,levels=c(1,0),  
                              labels=c("Smoker","Non-Smoker")))

#Prints dataset to view modifications
head(periodontal.data)
```

#### Census Tract Data Loading, Processing, and Consolidation

For the 2014 and 2017 census-tract data, it will be loaded in through a GitHub link from the data uploaded onto the repository. The data contains a lot of unnecessary data and will have to be filtered to contain data on smoking prevalence ("CSMOKING_CrudePrev") only in the city of Philadelphia. Census tract data such as FIPS code ("TractFIPS") will also be used for selected.

The "tracts" function from the `tigris` package is utilized to select and load in the geospatial coordinates ("GEOID" and "geometry" variables) for Philadelphia from 2014 and 2017, respectively. The smoking prevalence and geospatial coordinate data is merged by using the GEOID/TractFIPS data.

```{r}
#Reads 500Cities_2014_CensusTractData.csv file
smoking.data.2014<-read_csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DannyTran0/BMIN5030_Final_Project/refs/heads/master/500Cities_2014_CensusTractData.csv")

#Visualizes data
head(smoking.data.2014)

#Filters and selects relevant variables
philly.smoking.2014<-smoking.data.2014 |>
  filter(StateAbbr=="PA", PlaceName=="Philadelphia") |>
  mutate(TractFIPS=str_pad(as.character(TractFIPS),
                         width = 11)) |>
  select(TractFIPS,CSMOKING_CrudePrev)

#Variable meaning
#StateAbbr: Abbreviation of U.S. state
#Place Name: Name of U.S. city
#TractFIPS: Designated FIPS code for an area of the cities
#CSMOKING_CrudePrev: 2014 data of smoking prevalence in a particular area of each city

#Checks that everything has been correctly done
head(philly.smoking.2014)
dim(philly.smoking.2014)
```

```{r}
#Loads in 2014 tract data of Philadelphia
philly.tract.2014<-tracts(state="PA",
                          county="Philadelphia",
                          year=2014) |>
  select(GEOID,geometry)

#Merges the geospatial coordinates from the 2014 tract data into smoking data using GEOID
philly.2014<-philly.tract.2014 |>
  inner_join(philly.smoking.2014,
             by=c("GEOID"="TractFIPS"))

#Checks that everything has been correctly done
head(philly.2014)
dim(philly.2014)

class(philly.2014)
```

```{r}
#Reads 500Cities_2017_CensusTractData.csv file
smoking.data.2017<-read_csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DannyTran0/BMIN5030_Final_Project/refs/heads/master/500Cities_2017_CensusTractData.csv")

#Visualizes data
head(smoking.data.2017)

#Filters and selects relevant variables
philly.smoking.2017<-smoking.data.2017 |>
  filter(StateAbbr=="PA", PlaceName=="Philadelphia") |>
  mutate(TractFIPS=str_pad(as.character(TractFIPS),
                           width = 11)) |>
  select(StateAbbr,PlaceName,TractFIPS,CSMOKING_CrudePrev)
  
##Checks that everything has been correctly done
head(philly.smoking.2017)
dim(philly.smoking.2017)
```

```{r}
#Loads in 2017 tract data of Philadelphia
philly.tract.2017<-tracts(state="PA",
                     county="Philadelphia",
                     year=2017) |>
  select(GEOID,geometry)

#Merges the geospatial coordinates from the 2017 tract data into smoking data using GEOID
philly.2017<-philly.tract.2017 |>
  inner_join(philly.smoking.2017,
             by=c("GEOID"="TractFIPS"))

#Checks that everything has been correctly done
head(philly.2017)
dim(philly.2017)
```

Smoking prevalence data from 2014 and 2017 is taken and consolidated into its own table. A new column is added into the table in "philly.smoke.data.consolidation.2017" to show the change in smoking prevalence between 2014 and 2017.

```{r}
#Stores smoking prevalance data
philly.smoke.change.2014<-philly.smoking.2014$CSMOKING_CrudePrev
philly.smoke.change.2017<-philly.smoking.2017$CSMOKING_CrudePrev

philly.2017<-philly.2017 |>
#Adds a new variable about a change in smoking prevalence between 2014 and 2017
  mutate(smoke.prevalence.change=philly.smoke.change.2017-philly.smoke.change.2014)
```

#### Data Visualization

placeholder

```{r}
#Selects the relevant variables
smoker.gender<-select(periodontal.data,gender,smoker.status)

#Creates a bar plot visualizing a participant's smoker status based on gender
ggplot(smoker.gender,aes(x=gender,fill=smoker.status))+
  geom_bar()+
#Labels the x-axis, y-axis, and title for the plot
  labs(x="Gender",y="Number of Participants",title="Smoker status of participant based on gender")+
  theme_bw()+

#Creates a bar plot visualizing a participant's smoker status based on age

  dplyr::filter(!is.na(age)) #Filters out missing data
#Creates a bar plot visualizing a participant's smoker status based on their age
ggplot(smoker.age,aes(x=age,fill=smoker.status))+
  geom_bar()+
  labs(x="Age",y="Number of Participants",title="Smoker status of participant based on age")+
  theme_bw()+
  theme(plot.title=element_text(hjust=0.5))

#Creates a bar plot visualizing a participant's smoker status based on education
smoker.education<-select(periodontal.data,education,smoker.status)
#Creates a bar plot visualizing a participant's smoker status based on their education
ggplot(smoker.education,aes(x=education,fill=smoker.status))+
  geom_bar()+
  labs(x="Education Level",y="Number of Participants",title="Smoker status of participant based on education")+
  theme_bw()+
  theme(plot.title=element_text(hjust=0.5))
```

#### Bivariate and Multivariate Analysis between ...

```{r}
#Bivariable Analysis

#Runs a bivariate analysis to determine the relationship between the outcome variable 
#(percentage of detected periodontal disease) and predictor variable (smoker status)
peri.smoke<-lm(percent.peri.detected~smoker.status,
                data=periodontal.data)

#Summarizes bivariate analysis data of detected periodontal disease and smoker status
summary(peri.smoke)
#
confint(peri.smoke)

#Organizes output of bivariate analysis
modelsummary(peri.smoke,statistic="p.value")
```

```{r}
#Multivariate analysis

#Runs a multivariate analysis of detected periodontal disease, smoker status, and age of participant
periodontal.age<-lm(percent.peri.detected~smoker.status+age,
                    data=periodontal.data)
summary(periodontal.age)

#Runs a multivariate analysis of detected periodontal disease, smoker status, and gender of participant
periodontal.gender<-lm(percent.peri.detected~smoker.status+gender,
                           data=periodontal.data)
summary(periodontal.gender)

#Runs a multivariate analysis of detected periodontal disease, smoker status, and education level of participant
periodontal.education<-lm(percent.peri.detected~smoker.status+education,
                           data=periodontal.data)
summary(periodontal.education)

#Runs a multivariate analysis of detected periodontal disease, smoker status, and age, gender, and education level of participant
periodontal.all<-lm(percent.peri.detected~smoker.status+age+gender+education,data=periodontal.data)
summary(periodontal.all)
```

```{r}
#here is a map
#Customizes aspects of a plot
my_theme <- function() {
  theme_minimal() +                                  
    theme(axis.line = element_blank(),                 
          axis.text = element_blank(),                 
          axis.title = element_blank(),
          panel.grid = element_line(color = "white"),  
          legend.key.size = unit(0.8, "cm"),          
          legend.text = element_text(size = 7),       
          legend.title = element_text(size = 7),
          plot.title = element_text(size = 12))      
}

myPalette<-colorRampPalette(brewer.pal(9,"YlOrRd"))

prev.max.2014<-max(philly.2014$CSMOKING_CrudePrev)
prev.min.2014<-min(philly.2014$CSMOKING_CrudePrev)

ggplot()+
  geom_sf(data=philly.2014,lwd=0,aes(fill=CSMOKING_CrudePrev))+
  ggtitle("Smoking Prevalence in Philadelphia in 2014")+
  scale_fill_gradientn(name="Smoking Prevalence (%)",colours=myPalette(100),limit=range(prev.max.2014,prev.min.2014))+
  my_theme()
```

```{r}
#Static map
prev.max.2017<-max(philly.2017$CSMOKING_CrudePrev)
prev.min.2017<-min(philly.2017$CSMOKING_CrudePrev)

ggplot()+
  geom_sf(data=philly.2017,lwd=0,aes(fill=CSMOKING_CrudePrev))+
  ggtitle("Smoking Prevalence in Philadelphia in 2017")+
  scale_fill_gradientn(name="Smoking Prevalence (%)",colours=myPalette(100),limit=range(prev.max.2017,prev.min.2017))+
  my_theme()
```

Based on the choropleth maps, it shows that the smoking prevalence is concentrated in the North and West Philadelphia areas for both 2014 and 2017. A slightly noticeable difference is observed in the 2017 map, particularly with the West Philadelphia area, ...

```{r}
#Leaflet map

#Bins continuous variables into an ordinal color scale appropriate for our data
palette.map<-colorNumeric(
  palette=c("green","yellow","red"),
  domain=philly.2017$smoke.prevalence.change
)

#Creates a pop-up message containing county name, state name, and obesity rate change as a percentage
pu.message<-paste0("<br>Change in Smoking Prevalence (2014-2017): ",
                   philly.2017$smoke.prevalence.change,
                   "%")

#Creates an interactive choropleth map of the obesity rate change in each U.S. county
leaflet(philly.2017) |>
  addPolygons(stroke=F,                       #Removes polygon borders
              fillColor=~palette.map(philly.2017$smoke.prevalence.change), 
              fillOpacity=0.7,                #Increases opacity
              smoothFactor=0.5,               #Increases resolution
              popup=pu.message) |>            #Adds pop-up message
  addLegend("bottomright",                    #Places legend in designated location
            pal=palette.map,                   #Palette function
            values=~smoke.prevalence.change,  #Variable to pass palette function
            title="Smoking Prevalence Change (%)",  #Title of legend
            opacity=1) |>                     #Legend opacity
  addScaleBar()                               #Adds distance scale
```
